# dryad_group (Resource)

Manages an Active Directory group by executing PowerShell on a remote Windows host.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dryad_group" "server_admins" {
  name             = "Server Admins"
  sam_account_name = "SERVER-ADMINS"
  path             = "Contoso/Groups"
  description      = "Administrators of all servers"
  category         = "Security"
  scope            = "Global"
}

# path also accepts a DN relative to the domain root, for containers that are not OUs.
resource "dryad_group" "legacy_readers" {
  name  = "Legacy Readers"
  path  = "CN=Users"
  scope = "DomainLocal"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Group name (the `CN`). Changing this renames the group in place.
- `path` (String) Container holding the group. Accepts a slash-delimited OU path relative to the domain root (`Contoso/Groups`), a distinguished name relative to the domain root (`CN=Users`), or a full distinguished name. Changing this moves the group.

### Optional

- `category` (String) Group category: `Security` or `Distribution`.
- `description` (String) Group description.
- `sam_account_name` (String) Pre-Windows 2000 group name. Defaults to `name`.
- `scope` (String) Group scope: `DomainLocal`, `Global` or `Universal`.

### Read-Only

- `distinguished_name` (String) Distinguished name of the group. Changes when the group is renamed or moved.
- `id` (String) Terraform resource identifier. Equals the group `objectGUID`, which is stable across renames and moves.
- `sid` (String) Security identifier of the group.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Groups are imported by objectGUID, which is stable across renames and moves.
terraform import dryad_group.server_admins "9cb8219c-31ff-4a85-a7a3-9bcbb6a41d02"
```
